title: Dioxyzine Frog
summary: A storefront for custom plushies, dolls and accessories.
role: Frontend development and service integration, including backend parts of checkout and order management.
introduction: I’m building an e-commerce website for custom plushies, dolls and accessories. The project connects a customer-facing storefront with accounts, order tracking and administration workflows.
problem: Keep product discovery, checkout and order follow-up connected in one website, while making the administration tools usable for the shop.
features: Product listings, product details and a shopping cart
Account registration, sign-in, password reset and profile pages
limits: Repository documentation does not certify every production integration as fully verified.
outcome: A documented web application spanning storefront, accounts, checkout and order workflows.
learningFocus: Tracing checkout through the UI, payment capture and stored order state.
Connecting account and admin flows to database access rules.

title: Frog Management
summary: A staff app for workshop operations at The Frog Art Space.
role: Building the staff interface, business workflows and Supabase-backed operations.
introduction: I’m building a staff-only application to replace workshop spreadsheets with one place for events, counter sales, tickets, queues, inventory and reporting.
problem: Connect the steps of running a workshop event so staff can work with the same ticket, order and stock information.
features: Counter orders, tickets and queue display
status: Phase 1 source; live acceptance testing pending
limits: The first business unit is a workshop with a small F&B catalogue; a separate cafe workflow has not been built.
Hosted authentication, real-device updates and physical printing still need acceptance verification.
The repository also contains a separate mock frontend prototype.
demoLabel: No verified public demo linked in this study
outcome: An initial implementation with documented business rules, database changes and an acceptance checklist.
learningFocus: Turning order, stock and ticket states into explicit business rules.
Separating paid revenue, cost and profit in reporting.

title: Retail Customer Insights
summary: Historical transactions explored through SQL, RFM and a dashboard.
role: Data cleaning, metric definitions, SQL analysis and dashboard presentation.
introduction: I built this case study to practise working with transactional data from cleaning through to analysis. It uses the historical UCI Online Retail dataset and presents the results in Streamlit.
problem: Understand sales patterns and customer behaviour while making the cleaning rules and limits of the dataset visible.
features: SQL business questions and a local SQLite export
A data-quality audit and documented metric definitions
limits: Revenue from retained positive sales is not profit or net revenue after returns.
RFM segments are descriptive rules, not a trained churn model.
outcome: A dashboard, reproducible cleaning rules, SQL queries and documented limitations.
learningFocus: Defining metrics and cleaning rules before building charts.
Keeping missing customer IDs separate from transaction-level sales.

title: World Cup Player Analytics
summary: Player events and comparisons within a selected World Cup match.
role: Event aggregation, metric definitions and interactive player comparisons.
introduction: I built a small dashboard to explore player event statistics from the 2022 World Cup. It loads StatsBomb Open Data and compares players within one selected match.
problem: Turn event records into understandable player summaries without overstating what those records can measure.
features: Select a match from the 2022 World Cup
Explore goals, assists, shots, passes and pass accuracy
Compare two players from the same match
limits: Metrics are for the selected match, not the whole tournament.
The current version does not estimate verified minutes or per-90 statistics.
It does not predict match outcomes or rank overall player quality.
demoLabel: Run instructions available in the repository
outcome: An interactive player dashboard with documented event definitions and synthetic regression tests.
learningFocus: Defining player metrics from event records.
Handling zero attempts and excluding penalty-shootout events.
